messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Table like dotplot
parts:
One (not very elegant) way to do it is to make the whole table with ggplot2. This should get you most of the way there:

library(ggplot2)

data <- read.table(header=TRUE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE, con <- textConnection('
id    Col1  Col2  Col3  Col4
 1   "foo"    25   1.1  .001
 2   "bar"    44   0.5    .3
 3  "more"    84   .23   .01
 4 "names"    35    -3    .6
 '))
close(con)



ggplot(data, aes(x=Col4, y=id)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept=0,   colour="black") +
    geom_vline(xintercept=.05, linetype="dashed", colour="grey70") +
    geom_vline(xintercept=.1,  linetype="dashed", colour="grey70") +
    geom_vline(xintercept=1,   linetype="dashed", colour="grey70") +
    geom_point() +
    annotate("text", x=-.4, y=5, label="Column 1", 
             hjust=1, vjust=1, # Right, top alignment
             fontface="bold") +
    geom_text(aes(label=Col1), x=-.4, hjust=1) +  # Right align

    annotate("text", x=-.25, y=5, label="Col\n2", hjust=1, vjust=1, 
             lineheight=.8,  # Bring lines closer together
             fontface="bold") +
    geom_text(aes(label=Col2), x=-.25, hjust=1) +

    annotate("text", x=-.05, y=5, label="Col\n3", hjust=1, vjust=1, 
             lineheight=.8,  # Bring lines closer together
             fontface="bold") +
    geom_text(aes(label=Col3), x=-.05, hjust=1) +

    theme_bw() +
    scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-.6,1), breaks=c(0, .05, .1, 1)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(1,5)) +
    opts(axis.text.y  = theme_blank(),
         axis.title.y = theme_blank(),
         axis.ticks   = theme_blank()) +
    opts(panel.grid.minor = theme_blank(),
         panel.grid.major = theme_blank())


There are some text properties that might be useful but aren't well documented at this point: hjust, vjust, rot (angle), fontsize, fontfamily, fontface, and lineheight.

Also, I think some of the things I did here also require the development version.
https://gist.github.com/1150934

-Winston
